## Natural history notes

A large, nonvenomous snake characterized by its long, slender body, dark blotched or mostly black coloration, and pale belly with darker markings. In Florida, it is found in a wide variety of habitats including hardwood forests, pine flatwoods, hammocks, swamps, agricultural areas, and suburban landscapes. It is an excellent climber and feeds mainly on rodents, birds, and eggs, often occurring around trees, barns, sheds, and other areas where prey is abundant.
